# IT Enterprise Governance site: create the lists from CSV

<!-- Generated by SharePointGovernance/tools/build_list_csvs.py from the solutions' list-schema.json. Don't edit. -->

For Site Owners without the PnP provisioning scripts (no client ID needed). Each CSV makes one list with the columns the flows expect. The provisioning scripts do the same thing automatically, so use one route or the other, not both.

## How to import a list

1. On the site, select **New > List > From CSV** (or **Lists > New list > From CSV**) and pick the file.
2. Name the list **exactly** as given below. The flows find lists by name.
3. In the preview, set each column's **type** from the table. Leave the column names as the
   headers (they are the internal names the flows use). If a column offers a choice of title
   column, use **Title**.
4. **Create.** Then, in the list:
   - delete the EXAMPLE rows
   - in **List settings**, for each column: rename it to the display name in the table, tick
     *Require that this column contains information* where Required says Yes, set the default,
     and check the choices
   - hide the columns marked *hide from the new / edit form* (*Edit columns* on the form, or
     the column's settings)
   - add the columns marked *add by hand*
   - index the columns marked *index it* (*List settings > Indexed columns*)
   - turn on **Versioning** (*List settings > Versioning settings*)
5. **Check the internal names.** Open each column's settings: the address ends `Field=<internal
   name>`, which must match the table exactly. A header SharePoint already uses gets a number
   added (for example `Category0`). If that happens, delete the column and add it by hand with the
   internal name.

Create lists that others look up first (the order below already does this).

## SharePointGovernance

### Site Register

One row per SharePoint Online site. Source of truth for owners, security groups, sharing and sensitivity. Site access reviews are SAM site attestations (D-GSA-08). New sites are added by flow 03; sites that existed before these flows were introduced are bulk-loaded once.

**CSV:** `Site_Register.csv`. *New > List > From CSV*, name the list exactly **Site Register**, then set each column's type as below. After it's created, delete the 4 EXAMPLE rows.

| CSV header = internal name | Type to choose | Then rename to | Required | Choices / default | After import |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SiteTitle` | Single line of text | Site title | Yes |  |  |
| `SiteUrl` | Single line of text | Site URL | Yes |  |  |
| `Department` | Single line of text |  |  |  |  |
| `PrimaryOwner` | Person | Primary owner | Yes |  |  |
| `SecondaryOwner` | Person | Secondary owner | Yes |  |  |
| `OwnersGroupId` | Single line of text | Owners group (Entra object ID) | Yes |  |  |
| `MembersGroupId` | Single line of text | Members group (Entra object ID) | Yes |  |  |
| `VisitorsGroupId` | Single line of text | Visitors group (Entra object ID) |  |  |  |
| `GuestsGroupId` | Single line of text | Guests group (Entra object ID) |  |  |  |
| `SharingCapability` | Choice | External sharing | Yes | Disabled, ExistingExternalUserSharingOnly; default Disabled |  |
| `Sensitivity` | Choice |  | Yes | General, Confidential, Highly Confidential; default General |  |
| `Status` | Choice |  | Yes | Active, Orphaned - owner inactive, Read-only, Archived; default Active |  |
| `LastAccessReview` | Date and time (include time) | Last access review |  |  |  |
| `NextAccessReview` | Date and time (include time) | Next access review |  |  |  |
| `UrgentAlertKey` | Single line of text | Urgent alert sent for |  |  |  |

**CSV:** `Access_Requests.csv`. *New > List > From CSV*, name the list exactly **Access Requests**, then set each column's type as below. After it's created, delete the 12 EXAMPLE rows.

## ISO 27001

ISO 27001 controls go in the **Compliance Register** above (Framework = ISO 27001). There is no separate ISO list.
